title: Welcome to Brick by Script
summary: Find your starting point, understand the studios and make your first small change.
body: One workspace for your next idea Brick by Script is a Windows desktop workspace for FiveM creators. Use Script Studio to work on Lua resources and interfaces, or MLO Studio to build an editable interior. Clothing, Jewelry and Vehicle studios provide workspaces for supported wearable and vehicle workflows. You do not need to understand every tool before you begin. Start with one task: move a doorway in the example house or change a greeting in the guided chat project. Core editing and these practice activities work offline. Find your way around the new workspace The top bar is shared across the app. Home resumes your current project and shows recent work. Projects opens the local library. Studios switches between Script, MLO, Clothing, Jewelry and Vehicle studios. Tools keeps the other workspaces, including Pack Builder, fitting, asset browsing and project transfer, within reach. Learn opens guided help. Use New project on Home or in Projects to choose one of the five project types. Existing work stays in the same library. Use the top-right Workspace settings control for preferences and updates, or press Ctrl+K to search commands. Beginner exercises and backups are still on Home; scroll below Recent projects to find them. The command palette also retains Getting started as a route back to Home. Choose a starting path New to the app? Follow Install on Windows , then Your first project . Already use Brick by Script? Follow Update the app to choose the right update path for your installed version. Interested in code? Start with Script Studio . Bringing a design from another computer? Learn how to save and move your projects . Read What’s new for the latest changes. You can keep using your existing project library after an application update. Set up your workspace , or use an optional GitHub account to continue on another PC . Know which version you are using The public download is 0.21.0 alpha . These guides cover that release, including Clothing, Jewelry and Vehicle studios. If you installed an older version, use the installation guide to update. The app is still in alpha development. The installer is unsigned, and clean-device, laptop and owner-run in-game acceptance remain pending. A successful preview or export does not prove that a resource works in game. The export guide explains the steps between an editable design and a tested FiveM resource.

title: Install on Windows
summary: Install for the first time, update an older copy, or take your workspace to a laptop.
body: Choose the published download Select Download Brick by Script for Windows to download the 0.21.0 installer directly. This is the current Windows x64 alpha prerelease. You do not need to find the file in a GitHub Assets list. The release notes describe this version and its known limitations. The installer is unsigned, and clean-device and laptop acceptance remain pending. If Windows blocks the file, keep the exact message for troubleshooting; these instructions do not require disabling Windows security. Install and open Find Brick-by-Script-0.21.0-Setup.exe in your browser’s downloads or your Downloads folder. Open the installer and complete the installation, then launch Brick by Script. Open Home . Choose Open example house or Make a chat command to check that the workspace opens. Expected result: the app opens an editable example or a guided practice project. You do not need Blender or a running FiveM server for this first check. Keep your work when updating Already on 0.18.0 or later? Open Workspace settings → App updates , or press Ctrl+K and choose App updates . Follow Update the app to check releases, download and choose when to restart. On 0.17.1 or earlier? Download the current installer once to add the updater. Save your changes, create an editable project backup and close the older app before running it. After setup, launch Brick by Script from the Windows Start menu, then open Workspace settings → App updates to confirm the installed version. For another PC, transfer your project backups as well as the installer. Portable folders and development copies cannot use in-app installation; use the Windows setup version. Keep portable runtime files together rather than copying only the executable. A copy launched with a custom workspace profile also cannot install in-app updates; open the installed app normally to use that flow. The installer updates application files while the project library stays in its existing Windows profile. A project backup remains a separate copy of your editable work. The release provides SHA256SUMS.txt for checking manual downloads; in-app downloads verify the published file size and SHA-256. This verifies file integrity, not publisher signing.

title: Update the app
summary: Find your update path, download while you work and restart when you are ready.
body: Find the updater Open Workspace settings → App updates . You can also press Ctrl+K , search for App updates and select the command. The panel shows your Installed version and update channel. 0.18.0 or later, installed with Windows setup: use the steps below. Open the installed app from the Windows Start menu. 0.17.1 or earlier: the old app has no updater. Download the current Windows installer , save and close the older app, and install once. Future updates can use this panel. Portable or development copy: the panel can check releases but cannot download or install them. Run the Windows setup installer to use in-app installation. Custom workspace profile: installation is unavailable when the app was launched with a custom --user-data-dir . Open the installed app normally. Your custom profile is not moved or deleted. See Install on Windows if you need help finding the installer or opening the installed copy. Check and download Select Check for updates . This needs an internet connection. If a newer compatible release appears, read its version and notes. Select Download update . Watch its progress, or choose Keep working to close the panel and continue editing while the download runs. Open App updates again, or select the update message in the bottom status bar, to return to its progress. Expected result: Your update is ready appears only after the download matches the published size and SHA-256. Checking and downloading do not install anything. If you see No newer updates found , you already have the newest compatible installer in the selected channel. You do not need to reinstall the same version. Cancel a download or reopen later Keep working closes only the update panel; a running download continues. Cancel download stops it. Closing the whole app also stops an unfinished download. Cancelled or interrupted downloads start again from the beginning when you retry; they do not resume from the previous percentage. Temporary partial files are cleaned up. If you fully downloaded an update but closed the app before installing it, reopen App updates and select Check for updates , then Download update . The app can reuse a complete cached installer for the selected release after verifying it again. If the file is missing, changed or belongs to another release, it downloads the selected installer instead. Install when you are ready Keep a project backup before an upgrade. After the download is ready, choose Install and restart… . Read the confirmation, then select Install and restart . Choose Keep working to wait. If autosave is off and there are unsaved changes, choose Save changes to keep them, Discard changes only if you do not want them, or Cancel to keep the app open. If a creative-tool task is running, choose whether to keep working or cancel the task before closing. Wait for installation and the app to reopen. Check Installed version in App updates, then reopen your project. The app finishes saving and closing before the installer replaces application files. Your library remains in its existing profile. The panel can show the last installation result; if reopening failed, launch Brick by Script from the Start menu and check that result. Choose when and what to check Check for updates when the app starts: off by default. Turn it on to check after a supported installed copy starts. It only checks; downloads and installation still need your action. Include preview releases: on by default for this alpha. The channel badge reads Stable + preview . Turn it off to use Stable updates only. These choices are saved for the next time you open the app. If no verified installer exists for your channel, the app tells you. During alpha development, stable-only checks may have no eligible release. Enable preview releases if you want the published alpha updates. If an update cannot finish What you see What to do next Connection, timeout or GitHub rate-limit message Check your connection. If GitHub is limiting requests, wait and try Check for updates later. Download or integrity-check failure Check available disk space, then choose Retry download . An unverified file is not offered for installation. In-app installation unavailable Read the explanation in the panel. Open the registered installed copy with its normal profile, or use the official Windows setup installer. Installation did not finish Keep your work saved, check the reported Windows exit code and retry. If it keeps failing, use the official installer and include that exact code in your issue report. Windows blocks the installer Keep the exact message for troubleshooting. SHA-256 verification does not make this unsigned alpha signed or bypass Windows application controls. The official release page has the installer and checksums. Follow Troubleshooting for reporting an issue. Core local editing does not require a successful update check.
headings: Find the updater Check and download Cancel a download or reopen later Install when you are ready Choose when and what to check If an update cannot finish

title: Make the workspace yours
summary: Use the Midnight Showroom settings sidebar to arrange panels, tune your editor and find recovery, tools and cloud projects.
body: Open workspace settings Choose the top-right Workspace settings control. The Midnight Showroom sidebar groups controls into Workspace , Editor , Recovery , Tools and Account & cloud , with App updates below. Choose a category, then use Done or Return to project when finished. These are preferences for this computer. Signing in does not copy your layout, tool installations or local settings to another PC. Changes save automatically; the footer remains reachable while the content scrolls in smaller windows. Arrange the workspace In Workspace , show or hide Explorer , Inspector and the Bottom panel . The workspace preview reflects those switches and shows source text from the current project. Use MLO properties → Left / Right to choose the side for that studio’s properties panel. Reset layout restores the layout defaults. It does not remove your projects. Set up the editor and shortcuts Choose an editor font size, wrap long lines and decide whether to autosave edits. The Editor tab also contains MLO transform shortcut assignments. Assigning a key that another transform already uses swaps the two assignments. With autosave off, save deliberately. When leaving unsaved work, read the Save / Discard / Cancel prompt. Recovery and Undo explains how those choices differ from checkpoints and backups. Find recovery, tools and cloud Recovery: keep useful checkpoints and restore earlier work as a separate local project. Tools: reopen workspace setup to review skill level, creative-tool paths and the default export folder. Account & cloud: sign in with GitHub and explicitly save or download private project snapshots. Read Continue on another PC . App updates: check releases, download and choose when to restart. Follow Update the app . Expected result: close and reopen settings to find your chosen local preferences again. No account is required to customize the editor.

title: Continue on another PC
summary: Sign in with GitHub, save a private project snapshot and get an independent local copy on your other computer.
body: What cloud projects do Cloud projects are optional snapshots you save deliberately . Editing a local project or enabling autosave does not upload every change. Choose Save to cloud when you want to make the saved project available to your account on another computer. Get local copy restores a separate local project. It never overwrites an existing local design. Keep editable backups as well; Project transfer remains available without a cloud account. Sign in with GitHub Install the current app on each Windows PC. Open Workspace settings → Account & cloud . Choose Continue with GitHub . Finish signing in and reviewing consent in your system browser, then return to the app. Use the same GitHub account on both computers. Check the account shown before saving or downloading. You do not create a separate Brick by Script password. If you want to stop, return to the app and choose Cancel sign-in . If GitHub sign-in is unavailable, local editing and project transfer still work. Save from the first computer Save your design and any linked Blender source files. In Account & cloud, choose the Local project . For a first upload, leave Cloud destination set to Create a separate cloud project . To add a version to an existing cloud project, select that destination deliberately. Choose Save to cloud and wait for the saved-version confirmation. The snapshot includes the saved project, embedded artwork and supported linked Blender sources packed by Project transfer. Only upload files you have permission to store. Save and correctly link sources before packing; missing or unsupported sources can prevent a complete transfer. Continue on the other computer Sign in with the same GitHub account and choose Refresh projects . Find the project and choose Get local copy . Choose a local folder for linked source files. Wait while the app downloads, verifies and restores the snapshot. Under Ready on this computer , open the restored project. Expected result: a new editable local copy appears. Your previous local projects stay intact. To send later edits back, save this local copy to the cloud destination again. Recovery checkpoints, collections, account credentials, computer-specific tool paths and installed tools are not transferred as workspace settings. Install and configure Blender or other tools separately on the second computer. Handle changes from two computers If another computer saved a newer cloud version after you selected your destination, the app refuses to replace it silently. Refresh the list and get that version as a local copy to review. Alternatively, choose Create a separate cloud project to keep both versions. This release has no automatic merge or background sync. The cloud list exposes the current version; it is not a browser for restoring arbitrary older snapshots. Manage storage and remove cloud copies This preview allows 512 MiB of reserved snapshot storage per account . Storage is reserved in 4 MiB chunks, and older saved versions count toward the allowance. A single packed snapshot can be up to 384 MiB, subject to the remaining allowance. A large project can fill the allowance after only a few saves. Use a cloud project’s Delete control and confirm Delete cloud project to remove that project and its saved cloud snapshots. Local copies on your computers are kept. Download or back up any version you need before confirming. If a deletion is interrupted, retry it. Clean interrupted uploads releases unfinished uploads older than two hours. It does not delete completed projects or recently active transfers. Understand privacy and current limits Local editing requires no account. When you choose GitHub sign-in, GitHub authenticates you and the app’s hosted Supabase service receives the identity needed for your account, including your email. Selected project snapshots are stored in that hosted service when you choose Save to cloud . Cloud projects are private to the owning account. The app stores the sign-in on this Windows profile using operating-system encryption. Sign out removes that saved sign-in, while local projects and saved cloud snapshots remain. Signing out is not account or cloud-project deletion. Real GitHub sign-in, encrypted-session reopening and a hosted script-project upload/restore have been tested between two independent app profiles on one computer. Acceptance on a second physical PC and representative large linked asset transfers is still pending. The app remains an unsigned alpha; a successful cloud transfer does not prove native export or in-game compatibility.
headings: What cloud projects do Sign in with GitHub Save from the first computer Continue on the other computer Handle changes from two computers Manage storage and remove cloud copies Understand privacy and current limits

title: Your first project
summary: Move a doorway in the example house, inspect it in 3D and reopen your saved work.
body: Start with the example house This exercise makes one visible change to an existing project. You will move a front door, inspect the change in 3D and save the editable house. It works without a FiveM server. Open Home . Choose Open example house . Choose Edit the example house to begin the guided tour. If you previously paused it, the control may say Resume example house tour . Follow the highlighted controls in the app. The tour uses the example’s rooms and openings, so begin with the supplied house rather than an unrelated project. Move the doorway in the floor plan Open Floor plan to see the rooms from above. Select the room named by the tour, either on the plan or in the Room menu. Under Openings , choose the door identified by the tour. Change Opening offset to slide the door along its wall. Use the suggested value and press Enter . Expected result: the opening moves along the selected wall. An offset describes where the opening sits on that wall; it does not change the whole room’s position. If the new location does not fit, choose a smaller valid offset and inspect the plan again. Check the change and save it Open Scene view . In Perspective view, choose Frame selection or scene . Drag an empty part of the viewport to orbit around the doorway. Save your edited house. Wait until the app reports the saved state. Return to Projects and reopen your saved copy. Expected result: the reopened house keeps your new doorway position. You have completed an editable project, not an in-game acceptance test. Continue with a project backup before experimenting further. Prefer a first coding task? Choose Home → Make a chat command . Change the greeting inside its quotes, then enter /hello in the simulated chat. The Script Studio guide takes you through that workflow.
headings: Start with the example house Move the doorway in the floor plan Check the change and save it Prefer a first coding task?

title: Learn by making
summary: 18 practical studio lessons with explanations, practice, troubleshooting and knowledge checks.
body: Practice beside your project Open Learn → Studio learning paths . Choose any studio and lesson. Read the explanation, try the three steps and answer the knowledge check. The existing eleven Lua lessons are still in the sidebar. Open … · keep lesson beside me opens the workspace with a collapsible practice panel. Project creation uses the normal dialog; no project is silently replaced. Return to the lesson to finish the knowledge check. Progress is saved on this PC, separately from projects, backups and cloud snapshots. Checkboxes are your own practice record, not automatic build or in-game verification. Lessons never lock professional features. Find the tools and character sources first if you need setup. Clothing Studio Meet your real GTA character Choose a male or female freemode character and identify the garment you will edit. The body is your fitting reference; the garment is the item you change. A model supplies shape and UV coordinates. A texture supplies the colors printed on that shape. Picking the matching body first prevents designing for the wrong fit. Freemode ped: The customizable GTA character. Male and female use different bodies and compatible clothing. Open Tools & models in Learn and follow the Blender, Sollumz and CodeWalker setup. Keep your GTA V Legacy installation available. Open Clothing Studio, choose Tops, T-shirts & hoodies and choose Male or Female under Fitting body. Click Set up GTA character and select your own GTA V Legacy folder when prompted. Use Front, Side and Back to inspect the loaded character. For another item, use Edit GTA clothing, choose a drawable and its original texture, then Edit selected GTA item. If a garment is already linked, read Change and keep artwork before switching. Expected result: A real local character and garment appear. The male or female selection matches your intended wearer. Setup is cached on this PC; other PCs need their own game files and setup. If it does not work: If setup fails, use Check installed tools. Select the Blender installation that has Sollumz enabled. Choose the Legacy folder containing GTA5.exe and x64v.rpf. A filename typed into a GLB dialog is not an existing model. Why choose the fitting body before designing? The garment must fit the intended body. A design can look correct on one body and clip on another. The body choice is part of the asset target. Try independently: Locate the Female option and explain which setup would need repeating on a second PC. You do not need to switch your current design. Recolor a shirt and place a logo Change a fabric color and position your own artwork while understanding UVs. The artwork canvas is a flat texture. UV coordinates tell the app which pixels belong on the chest, sleeves and back. A rectangle that looks centered on the canvas may cross a seam on the actual garment. Check the 3D result after each change. UV: The mapping between a flat image and the surface of a 3D mesh. Select your garment material for painting. In Design, click the Fabric color swatch and choose a color. For black use #101010. If an original diffuse image covers it, inspect the artwork layers: an opaque image can hide the color underneath. Choose Add text and enter a short word, or Add PNG for your own transparent logo. Select that layer and drag it on the artwork canvas. Use its size controls or resize handles to fit it within the chest area. Enable UV seams when working on an imported garment. Check Front, Side and Back; move the artwork away from seams or unintended surfaces. Undo one change and redo it to learn the recovery controls. Expected result: The selected garment shows the intended color and readable artwork. Changing the design does not recolor the body or every material in the scene. If it does not work: If color does not change, check the selected Paint material and whether an original image layer covers it. If the logo repeats or stretches, inspect the UV layout; shrinking the image cannot repair shared or distorted UVs. A logo is split across the chest and sleeve. What should you inspect? The UV layout and artwork placement. The texture is being mapped to multiple surface regions. Their UV boundaries determine the placement. Try independently: Create a second layout with smaller lettering. Compare both in 3D, then keep the one you prefer. Save a design and choose an export Distinguish an editable project, a PNG and a wearable resource. Saving the project preserves the editable layers. Export PNG texture makes an image, not a game-ready garment. A native wearable needs the correct model, matching textures and resource setup. Retexturing an existing item and building a new wearable are different workflows. YTD: A GTA texture dictionary containing named texture entries used by a model. Wait for Saved, then use Project backup to keep a separate editable copy. Reopen the project from Projects and confirm the lettering and colors are still editable. Export PNG texture to a working folder. For a supported existing GTA garment, save its original texture dictionary and use GTA texture dictionary → Retexture existing YTD to save an edited copy. Keep the original source. Open Pack Builder for a wearable resource. Select the correct body and item slot, supply the required native or prepared source files and run its checks. Stop at any unresolved build requirement; a PNG alone cannot pass as a native model. Expected result: You have an editable project and know which output you created. Only a successful native build and package should proceed to a FiveM test. If it does not work: A missing reference after moving PCs needs the same local source relinked or regenerated. A GLB preview does not preserve every GTA shader, skeleton or native property needed for export. Which output preserves editable lettering and image layers? The saved project or project backup. The project keeps the editing data. A PNG contains only the resulting pixels. Try independently: Explain to another person which file they need to continue editing and which files the server needs. Jewelry Studio Choose a chain and its wearer Separate the jewelry model from the character used to check its fit. A downloaded chain is geometry, not a character. It may arrive without a usable GTA skeleton, shader setup or correct scale. Start with one permitted accessory and inspect what was actually imported before planning an export. Reference body: A character shown beside your jewelry to judge size and placement. It is not part of the jewelry you export. In Jewelry Studio, choose Browse GTA jewelry for an accessory from your own Legacy installation, or Import jewelry GLB for a model you have permission to use. Choose the matching male or female fitting body. For an imported chain, use Load GTA fitting body. In the pattern editor, open Fitting reference and use its GTA body loader or your own reference GLB. Inspect Worn, Front and Side views. Identify whether you are editing a GTA accessory, an imported model, or a Studio pattern before changing its controls. Expected result: You can identify the chain and the body separately. A locally loaded GTA reference matches the intended wearer. If it does not work: If the chain fills the view, use the fit/frame control and inspect its scale. A generic imported chain may need preparation in Blender before native export. Find the matching body setup under Learn → Tools & models. Does importing a chain GLB also provide a GTA character? No, the fitting body is separate. A GLB contains only the scene exported into it. The app must load the fitting body separately. Try independently: Point out the model source and body choice without changing either. Fit jewelry from more than one angle Adjust placement and recognize clipping before export. A necklace can look correct from the front while passing through the chest or floating above it. Position changes move it, scale changes its size, and rotation changes its orientation. Make one small change at a time so you know what improved the fit. Clipping: Two visible surfaces intersecting, such as a pendant passing through a shirt. Use the worn preview and a representative shirt. Choose Front, then Side, and find the pendant relative to the chest. Use the controls available for your source to adjust placement and size. For imported jewelry, select the intended part before transforming it. Check the loop around the neck as well as the pendant. Compare the fit with a different outfit or supported pose. Undo an adjustment that makes the side view worse. Note any motion or attachment checks that still need Blender and FiveM. Expected result: The jewelry clears the reference outfit in the inspected views. This is a visual fit check, not proof of correct animated skinning. If it does not work: If moving the pendant also moves unrelated parts, inspect the part selection. If the item clips only while moving, inspect its weights and attachment in Blender and test in FiveM. Why inspect a necklace from the side? To check chest clearance and depth. Depth problems can be hidden in the front view. Try independently: Explain the difference between moving a chain forward and making the entire chain larger. Prepare a wearable, not just a preview Identify the required preparation for a chain, watch, ring or other accessory. The item category controls where a wearable belongs. A necklace, a watch and a pair of glasses do not all share the same component or prop slot. The finished item also needs supported materials, appropriate geometry and an attachment or rig suitable for its body. Skin weights: Values describing how much each bone influences a mesh vertex during movement. Save the design and its source. Identify the intended body, jewelry kind and corresponding component or prop target in Pack Builder. For an imported mesh, follow its preparation and Blender workflow. Check scale, orientation, materials and rig/attachment. Use the actual build diagnostics rather than assuming every GLB is directly convertible. Run the supported native build and package checks. Keep the diagnostic report. In FiveM, inspect the item while walking, turning and changing clothes before recording an in-game pass. Expected result: You can explain any remaining preparation and distinguish editor checks from an in-game result. If it does not work: An item that stays still while the character moves usually needs its rig or attachment investigated. A model that looks metallic in the editor can require different GTA shader settings. A static preview looks good. What remains unproven? Animation, attachment and in-game appearance. A static rendering does not exercise the game engine or character animation. Try independently: Write down three movements you will test and one clothing combination that could cause clipping. MLO Studio Understand a room in 2D and 3D Inspect editable architecture and understand dimensions before building. A floor plan describes where a room sits and how large it is. The 3D view shows the generated walls, floor and ceiling. Work in realistic dimensions: a room that looks attractive from a distant camera can still be too small to walk through. Transform: An object’s position, rotation and scale. Position moves it; scale changes its size. Open the example house as a learning project. Select a room and inspect its dimensions in the architectural controls. Switch between Floor Plan and Scene View. Move a corresponding architectural room slightly, then inspect how the other view represents the change. Undo the move. Check a doorway, wall thickness and floor height from an angle close to a player’s viewpoint. Expected result: You can identify the same room in both views and restore an experiment using Undo. If it does not work: If nothing appears, frame the scene and check hidden objects/layers. A free-standing mesh wall is not necessarily part of the architectural room data. Which operation changes an object’s size? Scale. Scale changes size; position changes location. Try independently: Estimate a doorway width before inspecting its actual dimensions. Explain why scale matters for a player. Connect rooms with real portals Distinguish a visible doorway from room visibility data. A hole in a wall lets you see through the geometry in the editor. An MLO portal is separate data that connects room visibility in the game. A building can look complete while its room assignments or portals are missing. Portal: An opening definition connecting MLO rooms for visibility. It is not a physical door model. In MLO Studio, open Rooms and Portals. Identify two neighboring rooms and the doorway between them. Inspect the portal’s room connections, corners and direction. Use the connectivity view to find whether each intended interior route is connected, including the exterior/limbo relationship. Run the available room and portal diagnostics. Record one issue and its proposed correction, or explain why the selected doorway’s connection is sensible. Expected result: The portal lies at the intended opening and connects the correct rooms. You understand that visibility still needs a game test. If it does not work: If a room disappears from an expected viewpoint, inspect connections, portal direction and entity room assignment. Do not fix visibility by randomly adding overlapping portals. Does cutting a hole in a wall automatically prove MLO visibility is correct? No, portal data must be checked separately. Geometry and visibility definitions have different jobs. Try independently: Trace a player’s route from outside through two rooms and name every required visibility connection. Check collision and build requirements Find walkable surfaces and distinguish build checks from a game test. Visible geometry draws the room; collision controls physical contact. A rendered floor can have no collision, and an invisible collision surface can block a doorway. Inspect both before packaging. Collision mesh: The geometry the game uses for physical contact rather than visual detail. Open the collision workspace or overlay. Compare each floor and wall with its collision counterpart and check doorway clearance. Open Build and Export. Run diagnostics and inspect missing tools, room problems, materials and asset dependencies before starting the supported native build. After a successful build, inspect the generated resource and its manifest. Use a dedicated test server for entry, floor, wall, stairs and visibility checks. Record any checks you have not actually performed. Expected result: The project has an explained collision plan and an honest checklist of export and in-game requirements. If it does not work: Falling through a rendered floor points to collision loading or coverage. A successful ZIP operation only proves packaging, not gameplay. What proves the player can walk on a floor? A successful in-game collision test. The game must load and use the collision correctly. Try independently: Find one place where the visible model can be detailed but the collision can stay simple. Vehicle Studio Choose a vehicle with a usable source Identify the difference between a vehicle preview and a native source. A vehicle is more than a body mesh. A working GTA vehicle includes hierarchy, bones, materials, collision and configuration. A GLB can be useful for modeling or preview, but does not automatically contain those native relationships. YFT: A GTA fragment format used for vehicles and other structured assets. A ped skeleton can also use YFT; context matters. Open Vehicle Studio. Use Load GTA Blista for the supported car from your own Legacy installation, or import a permitted GTA fragment with its matching textures. Inspect Model overview and the parts hierarchy. Identify the body, a door and a wheel. Hide and show a part to understand the structure. Record the source kind. If you imported a GLB, inspect the native workshop requirements before expecting a driveable export. Expected result: You know what source the project uses and can select a vehicle part without confusing it with the whole car. If it does not work: Missing materials can mean matching YTD files were not supplied. A visual model alone does not establish a native vehicle structure. Does a car-shaped GLB necessarily contain a working GTA vehicle? No, native structure and configuration also matter. File extensions and appearance do not create the required internal data. Try independently: Identify one visible part and one nonvisual requirement for a working door. Change paint and place a livery Make a small visual change and verify its placement from several views. Paint settings and a livery image affect different parts of the material workflow. A logo is placed onto the model’s UV layout. Shared UV regions can repeat a logo, and stretched UVs can distort it. Livery: Artwork applied to a vehicle’s surface through its material and texture mapping. Open Customize and change the primary paint to a noticeably different color. Compare Front and Side views. In Livery, import your own PNG and choose Place logo on car. Select a supported panel, then adjust position, size and rotation. Inspect the opposite side and nearby seams for unwanted repetitions. Save, reopen the project and confirm the intended change remains. Expected result: The paint and logo are visible where intended, and you can explain which controls changed each. If it does not work: If a logo repeats across panels, inspect shared UVs. If native export reports an unsupported material, follow the diagnostic or prepare the source in Blender rather than assuming the preview can be exported unchanged. What can cause the same logo to appear on two panels? Shared UV coordinates. Two surface regions can sample the same pixels from a texture. Try independently: Try a smaller logo with more space around the edge of the panel and compare readability. Make one handling change and test it Use a controlled comparison instead of changing many settings at once. Handling fields interact. Changing acceleration, grip and braking simultaneously makes it hard to tell what helped. Preserve the original values, change one setting conservatively and compare on the same route. LOD: A level of detail: a different model complexity used at different viewing distances. In Configuration, inspect donor settings and give the add-on a unique spawn name. Record the original value of the one handling field you plan to change. Inspect Performance and Build pack for geometry, LOD, collision and missing dependency checks. Resolve build errors before packaging. In your dedicated FiveM test environment, compare the original and modified behavior on the same route. Check doors, wheels, lighting and distant appearance as well as driving. Expected result: You can describe one change and the evidence you would use to keep or revert it. Only mark the game test complete after driving it. If it does not work: A spawn failure may be configuration or naming, not the visible model. Inspect resource logs and manifest/configuration references before changing geometry. How do you learn which handling change caused a problem? Change one value and compare under the same conditions. A controlled comparison makes the effect attributable to that change. Try independently: Write a short driving test with the same vehicle, route and starting conditions. Script Studio Build a command and explain every part Create a command while understanding its name, callback and execution side. RegisterCommand connects a typed name to a function. The function is the callback: it runs when the command is used. The resource manifest decides which Lua files run on clients and which run on the server. Callback: A function supplied to another function so it can be called when an event or command occurs. Open Make a chat command. Read the generated example before changing its command name and message. Predict which command the user will type and what output they should see. Run the available practice check and compare it with your prediction. Open the practice project in Script Studio. Find RegisterCommand and its manifest entry. Explain where the callback begins and ends. Expected result: You can point to the command name, message and manifest entry instead of only copying a recipe. If it does not work: If the command does not run in FiveM, confirm the resource is started and the correct file is declared in fxmanifest.lua. The practice environment does not reproduce every game native. RegisterCommand('hello', ...) registers which chat command? /hello. The first argument gives the command its name; chat adds the slash. Try independently: Rename the command and predict the result before running it. Continue with Lua foundations for variables and functions. Find a bug using evidence Use a small reproduction, validation and a controlled fix. A useful bug report describes what you did, what you expected and what happened. A syntax check finds malformed code; it does not prove correct game behavior. Fix one observed problem and repeat the same steps. Reproduction: The smallest repeatable sequence that demonstrates a problem. Open a practice resource or a backup copy. Read its manifest and identify the expected entry script. Run validation and inspect any reported file and line. Compare the actual filename and command spelling with their references before editing. Make one correction, validate again and repeat the original action. Record any game-dependent checks you could not run locally. Expected result: You can explain why the correction addresses the reported issue and what remains untested. If it does not work: A clean validation result does not prove permissions, network events or game natives behave correctly. Use a development server and actual logs for those checks. What does a clean syntax check establish? The parsed code has no detected syntax errors. Parsing checks structure, not every runtime or security outcome. Try independently: Write a three-line report: steps, expected result, actual result. Understand resources and test safely Know what belongs in a resource and why the server validates requests. A FiveM resource groups its manifest and referenced files. Client code controls local presentation; the server must validate actions that affect shared state. A friendly button in a menu is not an authorization check. Dependency: Another resource or tool that must be available for the selected workflow to function. Inspect fxmanifest.lua and match each script or UI entry to an actual file in the project. For a script that changes shared state, identify where the server checks the caller and input. Read the Script security lesson if this is unfamiliar. Export the resource, read its requirements and test it on a dedicated development server. Keep your editable project backup separately from the deployment copy. Expected result: You can identify what the resource needs, where it runs and what tests are still required. If it does not work: A missing dependency needs the documented resource or a compatible implementation. Renaming arbitrary files does not satisfy an API or framework requirement. Where should a shared-state action validate player permission? On the server handling the request. A client can make requests independently of the visible interface. The server must enforce the rule. Try independently: Explain the difference between hiding a button and authorizing an action. Pack Builder Match a wearable to the right slot Choose the intended body and component or prop category. A clothing pack needs consistent targets. The wearer, item category, model and textures must agree. A hat and a shirt use different slots; choosing a slot does not convert an incompatible model into that item. Prop slot: A wearable category such as a hat or glasses, distinct from clothing component slots. Open Pack Builder and create or inspect a pack. Choose the intended male or female body. Add a supported item and select its correct component or prop category. Inspect its model and texture inputs. Review naming and dependency diagnostics before adding more items. Start with one item so failures remain easy to isolate. Expected result: One item has an explicit target and matching required files. Unsupported or missing inputs remain visible as unresolved requirements. If it does not work: If the wrong item appears in game, inspect the slot, collection and names before editing the artwork. Does selecting the hat slot turn a shirt model into a hat? No, the source must already be appropriate. The target describes the item; it does not remodel or rig its source. Try independently: Explain how you would classify glasses, a watch and a shirt without guessing a shared slot. Read build results correctly Separate missing inputs, conversion results and packaging results. A build is a sequence. Input validation checks source requirements. Conversion produces native assets through the supported toolchain. Packaging arranges the result as a resource. Each stage can succeed or fail independently. Native asset: A file encoded in the game’s actual supported format, not merely a renamed preview file. Run the pack checks and read every blocking diagnostic. Locate missing files or correct the target before building. Build through the supported workflow. Read the conversion result and check that the expected native files were generated. Export the resource to a chosen working folder. Inspect the manifest and stream contents and retain the build report. Expected result: You know which stages passed and can locate the exported files. No stage is assumed successful from a preview alone. If it does not work: A conversion failure needs its tool log or source fixed; retrying ZIP packaging cannot repair invalid native assets. What does successfully creating a ZIP prove? Files were packaged. Packaging does not run the game or prove the content works inside it. Try independently: List one failure that could occur at each build stage. Keep a repeatable in-game test record Record actual results for a wearable on the intended body. A release decision needs evidence from the intended environment. Keep automated checks separate from observations made in a running FiveM client. Use the same test actions when comparing revisions. Regression: A previously working behavior that breaks after a change. Prepare a dedicated test resource and note the app version, body, item and source revision. Follow the FiveM server setup guide if you do not have a test server. Load the resource and inspect the correct item on the intended character. Check textures, seams, body clipping and several movements. Record pass, fail or not tested for each check. After a correction, repeat the failing action and recheck behavior that already worked. Expected result: Your checklist describes tests you actually performed. Untested items remain marked not tested. If it does not work: If the resource does not load, inspect server logs and manifest paths first. A missing streamed asset and a badly fitting model require different fixes. You cannot open FiveM today. How should the movement test be recorded? Not tested. An honest unknown tells the next tester exactly what remains to be checked. Try independently: Prepare a reusable test list for another user and ask whether they can repeat it without your help.

title: Tools, downloads and character models
summary: Find official tool downloads and prepare real male/female GTA references from your own game.
body: Only set up what your workflow needs Open Learn → Tools & models or Tools → Tools & models in the app. Filter by studio, search for a tool and open the reviewed source page. Links open in your browser; the app does not automatically install tools. Lua lessons, Script Builder, NUI Designer, original scene editing and artwork practice do not need downloaded character models. Native asset workflows need compatible installed tools. Use Check installed tools / choose installations to inspect the selected Blender, Sollumz and CodeWalker setup. Male and female GTA character models The supported local setup prepares real mp_m_freemode_01 or mp_f_freemode_01 references from your own GTA V Legacy installation. There is no separate character GLB download to hunt for. Set up Blender with Sollumz and select CodeWalker. In Clothing Studio, select Male or Female under Fitting body, then Set up GTA character for tops. For other categories, use Edit GTA clothing. In Jewelry Studio, choose the matching fitting body. Use Fitting reference → Load from GTA installation in the pattern editor, or Load GTA fitting body for imported jewelry. When prompted, choose the Legacy folder containing GTA5.exe and x64v.rpf. Inspect the body and fit before editing. The generated reference stays on this PC. Repeat setup on another PC; caches are not included in public installers or project backups. A body reference does not automatically rig arbitrary clothing or jewelry. Game models are not redistributed with the app. Blender Free tool — Required by the automated model conversion and source-building workflows. Not needed to read lessons or edit Lua. Download a Windows version supported by your Sollumz release; the newest Blender release is not automatically compatible. Install and open Blender once. Then install Sollumz inside that same Blender installation. Use Check installed tools below and choose that blender.exe if the app detects a different installation. Official Blender downloads and LTS versions Sollumz Free Blender extension — Adds GTA asset support to Blender. Native import/export availability depends on the installed release/provider; use the app’s actual tool check. Follow the official installation guide for your Blender version. For Blender 4.2+, the guide documents adding https://repo.sollumz.org/ in Preferences → Get Extensions → Repositories. Choose the stable Sollumz extension. Enable it, then return to Brick by Script and check the same Blender installation. Read the reported native-workflow status before building. Sollumz installation instructions Sollumz releases and compatibility notes CodeWalker Free external tool — Used to read local GTA assets, inspect native files and support conversion workflows. Start at the developer’s project page and follow its published download route. Extract the complete tool folder. Keep CodeWalker.exe with its accompanying files. A repository source ZIP is not a compiled installation. In Check installed tools, choose CodeWalker from that folder. Point game browsing at your compatible GTA V Legacy installation. CodeWalker developer page and download route CodeWalker download page linked by its developer GTA V Legacy and local game assets Owned game required for game imports — Provides the male/female freemode bodies, stock clothing, accessories and donor vehicles used by local-game workflows. Original scene editing does not require downloading these assets. Install your owned GTA V Legacy copy through its official launcher or storefront. The local import workflows in this app require Legacy data. When prompted, browse to the folder containing GTA5.exe and x64v.rpf. Do not select the launcher executable or a shortcut. Use the character instructions below. No separate male/female GLB download is needed for the supported local setup. Keep game files local; they are not included in the public app or project backups. Official Rockstar launcher downloads Sollumz guide to male/female freemode components FiveM client Needed for in-game testing — Used to test the exported resource in the actual game. An editor preview is not this test. Follow the official client installation guide and its current game requirements. Join your dedicated development server after installing the test resource. Run the lesson’s in-game checklist. Record anything you have not tested as not tested. Official FiveM installation and client download guide FXServer and a development server Needed for resource testing — Runs resources for a FiveM client. Use a separate test environment; lessons do not deploy anything automatically. Follow the official server setup guide, which links the appropriate server artifacts and setup requirements. Configure a dedicated local test server and install only the resource you intend to test. Read server/client logs and repeat the same checks after a fix. Keep backups of your editable project outside the deployed resource. Official FiveM server setup and downloads Compatibility and source checks External references were checked November 17, 2026. Follow the selected release’s compatibility notes; the newest Blender is not automatically compatible with your Sollumz release. Opening a website is not a successful tool check. Native conversion and actual FiveM tests remain separate from lesson completion.
