title: Save, back up and move projects
summary: Organize your library, make independent copies, use recoverable Trash and take editable projects to another computer.
body: Use optional cloud snapshots In 0.19.0, Workspace settings → Account & cloud offers GitHub sign-in and private snapshots. Explicitly save a project, then get an independent local copy on another computer. Follow Continue on another PC for conflicts, storage limits and deletion. The backup and transfer workflows below remain available without signing in. Know which kind of copy you need Project library: the editable projects stored by the app on this computer. Use Ctrl+S to save and wait for the saved state. Project backup: a portable editable copy that you can restore into the app. Exported output: a texture, model, Blender file or resource package for another tool or the game. It is not automatically a complete project backup. Keep a backup before a major edit, an app update or a computer move. A backup stored only on the same drive does not protect you if that drive fails. Find and organize your projects Choose Projects in the top bar, or press Ctrl+O , to open the project library. Search by project name, folder label or tag. Use the studio and folder filters, Favorites , and the sort control to narrow the gallery. Use the star beside a project to favorite it. Choose its folder icon to edit Folder label and comma-separated Tags , then select Save project changes . A folder label organizes the library; it does not move files into a Windows folder. A project can have one folder label and up to ten tags. Clear the search and filters if a project seems to have disappeared. Choose New project to start a script resource, MLO interior, clothing design, jewelry design or vehicle project. Opening a card resumes that project. See a saved preview of your project Home and Projects show previews captured from the app’s own viewport after you open and save supported script, MLO, clothing, jewelry or vehicle work. Leave the workspace visible briefly after saving. A project without a current preview says Open to capture a preview . Previews stay on this computer, use bounded local storage and refer to the saved project revision. They are not source assets, backups or automatic cloud uploads. Editing a model requires a fresh preview after saving. Favoriting, renaming or organizing an unchanged project keeps its preview. The gallery avoids capturing open menus, dialogs and notifications. Reach project actions with a right-click In 0.19.1, right-click an entry in Project library to open it, rename it, duplicate it, favorite it, change its folder and tags, inspect recovery history or move it to Trash. Focus a project row and press Shift+F10 or the keyboard Menu key for the same menu. F2 opens Rename; Delete opens a Trash confirmation. In the Trash list, right-click an entry and choose Restore project . These actions use the existing save, confirmation and dependency checks. Moving an item to Trash remains recoverable and does not permanently delete it. Rename a project or make a separate copy Save the project first. Open the library and choose the pencil icon to Rename , or the copy icon for Duplicate / Save as . Enter a name starting with a lowercase letter. Use lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, with no spaces, up to 48 characters. Select Save project changes . After duplication, open the new entry from the library when you want to edit it; your original editor stays active. Renaming keeps the same project. Duplication creates an independently editable project with a new identifier. It copies saved design content and library folder/tags, but does not duplicate shared wearable collections or server jobs. Library management actions save pending edits in the active project before changing it. Linked Blender sources need the selected Blender installation so Studio can make and verify independent packed source copies. A missing file, tool or unsupported external dependency stops duplication with a message. Fix that source and retry; the original source file is not overwritten. Renaming does not rewrite resource names inside your scripts. Check explicit references after a rename. Folder, tag and favorite metadata belongs to this computer’s library and is not a portable project-design backup. Move unwanted projects to Trash and restore them In the All projects list, select the checkbox beside one or more entries. Choose Move selected to Trash and confirm. A single project also has a Trash icon in its row. To bring it back, open the Trash list, select the project and choose Restore selected . Return to All projects and open the restored entry. Expected result: the project leaves the ordinary list, then returns with its editable contents when restored. Trash keeps the project’s data and recovery history; it does not free disk space. This release has no permanent-delete command, and names in Trash remain reserved. If a wearable collection, server job or vehicle collection still references the project, Studio identifies the dependency and refuses the move. Remove the named reference first. A vehicle collection and its referenced projects can be selected together; restore its referenced projects before the owner, or restore them together. A blocked item leaves the whole selected batch unchanged. Keep a version before experimenting Open Workspace settings → Recovery → Project recovery to name and pin a checkpoint before a large edit. A checkpoint stays in this library; an exported backup is a separate file. The recovery and Undo guide explains which option to use, how to restore a selected project and how to discard unsaved edits. Save an editable backup Open the project you want to keep and save its current changes. Go to Home → Save project backup… . You can also use the project’s Project backup control where available. Choose a recognizable filename and a destination you can find again. Keep the supplied backup extension, such as .brickbyscript . Wait for the message confirming that the backup was saved. If the app reports that the project is too large or contains invalid data, address that message and create the backup again. A selected filename alone is not proof that a file finished saving. Reopen it on this or another PC Copy the backup to the destination computer and open a compatible version of Brick by Script. Choose Projects → Open backup . The same command is available as Home → Open project backup… . Select the saved backup. It is added to the destination library as a new project. Open the restored copy. Check its name, geometry or code, artwork and imported assets before you remove any original copies. Expected result: you can continue editing the restored project. Do not rename an ordinary model file to the backup extension; that does not turn it into a Studio project. Include the files your project depends on The current release also offers Project transfer for workflows with linked sources. Review its included and missing-file list. For Blender sources, pack the intended external images in Blender and save before transferring. Check the restored project on the destination machine. A local path that works on the first PC may be unavailable on the second. Source models, game installations and installed conversion tools can still require separate setup. Select a range and review its scope In 0.19.2, select a project checkbox, then Shift-click another checkbox or row to select the visible range. Ctrl-click toggles individual projects; Ctrl+Shift-click adds a range. Focus a row and use Shift+Up/Down to extend or shrink the selection. Ctrl+A selects the visible list while it is focused. Inside Search it still selects text. Filtering removes hidden projects from the selection, and sorting follows the visible order. Use Clear selection or Clear filters to reset the current scope. Ordinary project-button clicks still open the project. Bulk Trash confirmation lists the chosen projects. Right-click actions apply to the clicked project. Refresh reloads the library, and Retry lets you recover from a list-loading error without reopening the dialog.
headings: Use optional cloud snapshots Know which kind of copy you need Find and organize your projects See a saved preview of your project Reach project actions with a right-click Rename a project or make a separate copy Move unwanted projects to Trash and restore them Keep a version before experimenting Save an editable backup Reopen it on this or another PC Include the files your project depends on Select a range and review its scope

title: Recover work and use Undo
summary: Choose between Undo, unsaved changes, named checkpoints and backups without confusing what each one keeps.
body: Choose the kind of recovery you need Undo / Redo: move backward or forward through recent edits in the running app. Discard unsaved changes: return the current project to its last saved design. Recovery checkpoint: keep a saved version in the local library and restore it as a separate project. Project backup: create an editable file you can keep separately or move to another computer. Autosave is on by default, so an earlier edit may already be saved. Discard only affects changes that have not been saved. Use recovery or a backup when you need an older saved design. Choose Save, Discard or Cancel When autosave is off and the current project has unsaved edits, switching projects or closing the app asks what to do: Save changes: keep the pending edits and continue. Discard changes: return to the last saved design and continue. Cancel: stay where you are with the unsaved edits still available. To revert without leaving the project, press Ctrl+K , choose Discard unsaved changes… and confirm. Script Studio also offers this in its project menu. Already saved edits remain saved; there is no earlier version to discard if the app reports no unsaved changes. Save a named, pinned checkpoint Open the project you want to preserve. Choose Workspace settings → Recovery → Project recovery . Enter a Checkpoint name , such as “Before changing the fit.” Leave Pin this checkpoint selected if you want to protect it from automatic history cleanup. Choose Save checkpoint and wait for the confirmation. This saves the open project’s current edits first. To change an existing point, select it under Saved revisions , edit its name or pin status, and select Save checkpoint details . Restore the project you actually selected Press Ctrl+O and expand Recover an earlier project . Choose the correct entry in Project to recover , then expand Project recovery . Select the saved revision or named checkpoint you want. Choose Restore as new project . Find and open the recovered copy from the library to inspect it. The original project stays unchanged. Browsing another project’s history does not checkpoint whichever project happens to be open: Save checkpoint is disabled for an inactive project. Open that project first if you want to make a new checkpoint. Restore a project from Trash before browsing its earlier revisions. Recover an intact checkpoint from a damaged project In 0.19.3, damage to the latest project record no longer blocks its intact recovery history. If opening a project reports that its record is damaged, choose Open project library on the startup error screen, or open the library from another working project. Expand Recover an earlier project and choose the affected project. Expand Project recovery , select an intact saved revision and choose Restore as new project . Open the new copy and inspect its editable contents before continuing. The damaged original stays unchanged. This requires an intact checkpoint and a readable library; it cannot rebuild missing history or repair every kind of database damage. A project in Trash must be restored first, and a damaged checkpoint is still rejected. Recovery retains editable project data and embedded assets. It does not version linked Blender files. Use Project transfer for a separate backup of supported linked sources. Understand what history keeps Pinned checkpoints are protected from automatic cleanup until you unpin them. Limits are 8 pinned points per project , 128 across the library , and 64 MiB of pinned history . If pinning exceeds a limit, existing checkpoints remain unchanged; unpin an older point or export a backup. Unpinned history retains up to 12 recent points per project. All history shares a 128 MiB / 256-point library limit, so older unpinned points may be removed as new work is saved. Automatic points preserve the start and latest saved edit in each five-minute window. Naming or pinning the same saved revision does not create another copy of that revision. Recovery lives in the same local library as the project. Keep a separate project backup or transfer bundle for long-term storage and moving computers. Keep creator Undo across workspace changes Clothing Studio and Jewelry Studio keep separate Undo histories per project during the current app session. You can visit Pack Builder or Fitting and return to Undo or Redo. The history is bounded to 60 edits per creator, 12 recent creator histories and a shared memory budget; older history can be trimmed. Restarting the app starts a new Undo session. Saved designs and checkpoints persist separately. Discarding a design clears stale creator Undo, so Undo does not silently bring back the edits you chose to discard.
headings: Choose the kind of recovery you need Choose Save, Discard or Cancel Save a named, pinned checkpoint Restore the project you actually selected Recover an intact checkpoint from a damaged project Understand what history keeps Keep creator Undo across workspace changes

title: Start in Script Studio
summary: Edit your first chat command, move into the editor and understand what validation checks.
body: Make one command work in practice Open Home → Make a chat command . In client/commands.lua , find the greeting inside CityChat . Replace the words between the quotes and leave the quotes and parentheses in place. Enter /hello in the simulated chat. Follow the next step to rename the command to welcome , then try /welcome . Expected result: the simulated chat displays your message. In Lua, the command name is written without its leading slash; in chat, enter the slash. Use Show hint if you lose your place. Explore the resource files Choose Open in editor when you are ready to inspect the complete resource. Your guided practice draft remains on Home. A resource is a named folder that FiveM can start. Its fxmanifest.lua declares what it loads. Client files run for players, server files run on the server, and configuration files hold values the resource uses. For a fresh starter, choose Home → New project → Script resource (or use the New resource command) and choose a framework that matches your server. A QBCore starter depends on QBCore; it does not become standalone because you renamed the project. Save your changes with Ctrl+S . Add a file from your computer In Script Studio’s Explorer , choose New file… from the file or folder menu to open Add resource file . Select Browse files… . Use the Windows file picker to search your folders and choose an existing UTF-8 text file, such as a Lua script, JSON configuration or HTML page. Review File path . This is the destination inside your project, such as client/garage.lua . You can change it before adding the file. Starting from a folder keeps that folder as the destination prefix. Select Add file , review the imported text and save with Ctrl+S . The app copies the selected text into the project. It does not move or modify the original file, and it refuses to overwrite an existing project path. Cancelling the Windows picker keeps the dialog’s current selection. Choose Use empty file to create a blank file instead. Browsing supports text files; it is not a binary model, image or texture importer. Use the appropriate studio for those assets. Imported Unicode text, a UTF-8 byte-order mark when present, and line endings are retained. Add scripts to fxmanifest.lua when they should run, then validate the resource. Rename, move, copy or remove a file In Script Studio’s Explorer , open the three-dot action button beside a file or folder, or right-click its row. Choose Rename or move… , Duplicate… or Remove… . You can also focus a row and press F2 for rename/move, or Delete to open removal confirmation. For a move or copy, enter the complete destination path, such as client/garage.lua . A folder action includes its text files. Review the result and save with Ctrl+S . Conflicting or invalid paths are rejected without a partial change. Keep fxmanifest.lua at the resource root. These controls manage stored text files; imported binary assets remain managed by their studio. Before removal, Studio saves a recovery checkpoint. Use Restore removed files in Explorer to bring back the most recent removal during the current session. After restarting, use Project recovery to restore a checkpoint as a separate project. Review fxmanifest.lua , require / dofile paths and any HTML or CSS references after moving or removing files. Studio does not guess how to rewrite these references. Add copied files to the manifest when they should run or stream, then validate again. Right-click and keep your files close In 0.19.1, right-click inside the code editor for Cut , Copy and Paste . Ordinary editable text fields also offer native editing commands, with unavailable actions disabled. Selecting readable text outside an input offers Copy and Select all . Right-click a file or folder in Explorer for its actions, including New file… in that location and Copy relative path . The three-dot button gives you the same options without right-clicking. On a focused row, Shift+F10 or the keyboard Menu key opens the menu. Use arrow keys to choose an action, Enter to run it and Escape to dismiss it. Ctrl+W closes the active file tab. Middle-click a tab to close that tab. Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the most recently closed file tab in the current project. Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab move between open file tabs. Right-click a tab to close other tabs, tabs to its right or all tabs, or to copy its relative path. Closing a tab does not delete its file or discard its unsaved text. Closed-tab history belongs to the current project and app session; opening a different project clears it. Save the project before leaving or closing the app. Validate before exporting Choose Validate or press F5 . Read the reported problems. Select an item to open the relevant location. Correct syntax and manifest-path errors, then validate again. Choose Export ZIP when the resource is ready for a development-server test. Validation checks syntax, manifest references, execution side and common script problems. It cannot prove gameplay behavior or that a remote server has every dependency. See Export basics for the next boundary. A small standalone example For a separate practice resource, create a folder named brick-hello . Add this fxmanifest.lua at its top level: fx_version 'cerulean' game 'gta5' client_script 'client/main.lua' dependency 'chat' Create client/main.lua inside that folder: RegisterCommand('hello', function() TriggerEvent('chat:addMessage', { args = { 'Brick by Script', 'Hello from my first resource!' } }) end, false) This example uses FiveM's chat resource and needs it running. It is separate from the guided simulator's CityChat helper. Start the resource on your development server and enter /hello in game to check the message. Explore visual logic and interfaces The resource guide also covers Visual → Use starter flow and NUI → Use menu starter . Visual tools generate Lua; NUI tools build a game interface using web content. Their previews use sample data, so test the exported resource in FiveM. For the underlying chat event, use the official FiveM chat:addMessage reference . Move through dialogs and commands Press Ctrl+K to open the command palette and start typing. Use Up/Down to select a matching command and Enter to run it. In 0.19.3, keyboard selection scrolls into view, including when you wrap from the first command to the last. Dialogs place focus in their intended input after opening. Project-library search is ready for typing after its first load, unless you have already focused another control. Refreshing the library does not pull focus away from your choice. While a dialog such as Rename is open, global project shortcuts such as Ctrl+N stay blocked. Finish or dismiss the dialog before starting another project action. Escape closes a dismissible dialog; it does not cancel an operation that must finish safely. Resume your work and navigate files In 0.19.2, each project remembers open tabs, the active file, selection/cursor and editor scroll, plus its last project workspace. Closing all tabs keeps them closed when you return. Renamed files retain their remembered positions; missing files are ignored. The settings are local to this app profile, bounded to 24 recent projects, and do not travel with backups or cloud copies. Undo and closed-tab history remain session-only. Up/Down: focus the previous/next visible Explorer row. Right: expand a folder or enter it. Left: collapse a folder or focus its parent. Home/End: first/last visible row. Enter: open a file or toggle a folder. Type a visible file or folder name prefix to jump to it. Shift+F10 opens its actions. Ctrl+Shift+F searches file names and text. Use Next results and Previous results to move through pages of up to 100 matches. An empty search explains how to try again.
headings: Make one command work in practice Explore the resource files Add a file from your computer Rename, move, copy or remove a file Right-click and keep your files close Validate before exporting A small standalone example Explore visual logic and interfaces Move through dialogs and commands Resume your work and navigate files

title: Build your first interior
summary: Draw two connected rooms, add furnishings and keep an editable house project.
body: Start with a small house Begin with two rooms on one floor. That gives you a manageable project for learning walls, openings, furniture and visibility before you add multiple stories. For the quickest introduction, open Home → Open example house → Edit the example house . The public alpha includes this editable example. You can also create an MLO project and choose Beginner mode. Keep your first project separate from an interior you already rely on. Draw the layout Open Floor plan . Select Draw room , then drag from one corner to the opposite corner. The Add 5 × 4 m room button provides a precise starting size. Select the room and give it a useful name, such as Living room. Adjust its dimensions, wall height and materials in the room controls. Draw the second room against an existing edge. A shared wall makes the connection easier to inspect than two rooms that almost touch. Select Doorway and click the shared wall. Add another doorway on an outside wall for the entrance. Leave Create portal with new opening enabled when the opening should connect visibility. Switch to Scene view . You should see the generated floor, walls and openings corresponding to the plan. These architectural objects remain part of the same editable project. Use actions from the object hierarchy In 0.19.1, right-click an object in Scene objects to frame, duplicate, copy or paste the selection, group or ungroup it, change visibility or locking, isolate it, or request deletion. The menu respects locked objects and uses deletion confirmation. When you right-click an already selected object, selection actions apply to that selection. Focus an object row and press Shift+F10 or the Menu key to open its actions without a mouse. The hierarchy menu remains available. In 0.19.2: Right-click visible MLO geometry to open the object actions directly. Clicking an already selected object preserves the multi-selection. Architectural room geometry uses room-appropriate actions. Right-drag still controls the camera; dragging, pointer cancellation and releasing outside the canvas do not open a menu. Blank canvas provides applicable frame/show-all actions. Focus the canvas and use Shift+F10 for keyboard access. Furnish and inspect Open Asset browser , choose a room and place a piece of furniture. Return to Scene view , select it and use Move to adjust its position. Start with one table or chair so you can learn selection and camera navigation without a crowded scene. Use Collisions to inspect the solids that will stop a player. Use Rooms and portals to check how the rooms connect to the exterior. A visible doorway and its visibility portal serve different purposes. Keep background results tied to your scene In 0.19.3, a delayed import stays associated with the project that requested it. It preserves compatible newer scene edits instead of replacing the whole scene, and Undo returns to the actual state before that import. Switching projects cannot apply the result to the new project. Mesh previews check the target, operands, inherited transforms and calculation settings before they are applied. If you change those while a calculation is running, review the message and run it again from the current scene. Build results and design proposals identify the saved scene they used. A proposal cannot be applied to changed scene data, and walkthrough export checks the requesting project. Inspect the result's source and rebuild after relevant edits; a successful earlier build is not evidence for a changed scene. Collision edits also preserve the valid format of primitive-only scenes and work with generated architectural objects. Collision previews still require an actual FiveM walkthrough. Save before building Save the project, close it and reopen it from your library. Confirm that the room dimensions, doorway and furniture placement are still correct. Changing skill mode should expose additional tools without replacing the project. For a native build, choose the intended position in World placement , then review Build and test . Resolve reported errors and check the required tools before exporting. An attractive editor scene does not establish that collision or visibility works in FiveM. Continue with rooms and portals and the export workflow .
headings: Start with a small house Draw the layout Use actions from the object hierarchy Furnish and inspect Keep background results tied to your scene Save before building

title: Understand rooms and portals
summary: Connect an interior to the exterior and diagnose visibility problems without confusing portals with door holes.
body: Three separate parts of an entrance A door opening cuts the visible architectural shell. Collision determines whether the player can pass through that space. A portal connects room visibility. Creating or fixing one does not automatically prove the other two work. For a two-room house, the intended visibility route is usually exterior → first room → second room. The app calls the exterior relationship Exterior / limbo . It is not another furnished room that you need to draw. Create a connection In Floor plan , make sure the rooms meet at the intended wall. Select Doorway and click that wall. Enable Create portal with new opening before placing the doorway, or select an existing opening and enable Visibility portal . Inspect the opening's location and size. The portal should describe the opening you actually intend to see through, rather than an unrelated point in the room. Open Rooms and portals . Set Inspect connectivity from to Exterior / limbo , then inspect each room in turn. The connectivity graph and portal list should explain how the player sees into the house and between its rooms. Use them to find a missing connection before attempting another export. Check objects and direction Under Interior entity assignments , a placed mesh can use its geometry position or be assigned to a specific room. Check an object's assignment if it appears to belong to the wrong room or disappears at a doorway. The opening controls include Reverse portal direction . Inspect the portal's current relationship before changing it; reversing every portal is not a general repair for a visibility issue. Keep one change at a time so you can compare the result. Troubleshoot in order A wall still fills the doorway: inspect the opening in the floor plan and generated shell. The opening looks clear but blocks walking: inspect its collision solids. The next room disappears: inspect its portal connection, direction and entity assignments. A room is disconnected: trace a complete path from the exterior instead of only checking neighboring room names. Rebuild after correcting the project. In FiveM, check visibility from both sides of every portal and walk through each doorway. Record the result against the exact resource ZIP you tested, as described in the in-game checklist .
headings: Three separate parts of an entrance Create a connection Check objects and direction Troubleshoot in order

title: Edit real GTA clothing
summary: Set up a real male or female GTA character, choose a garment, place artwork and understand the steps to a native wearable.
body: Choose the right source Clothing Studio is included in public alpha 0.21.0. Start with a supported garment and keep its original files before making changes. In 0.20.1, Clothing Studio leads with Set up GTA character instead of the old bundled fitting person. The setup prepares a real male or female freemode character from your own GTA V Legacy installation. You do not need to find a wearable GLB first. Game models are not bundled with Brick by Script. The setup needs Blender with Sollumz and CodeWalker installed on your PC. Read Set up Blender and Sollumz before starting if these tools are not ready. Set up your first GTA character Create or open a clothing design. For the default top, choose Tops, T-shirts & hoodies under Item type. Choose Male or Female under Fitting body . Select Set up GTA character in the preview. On first use, choose your GTA V Legacy installation. If asked, locate CodeWalker from its complete installation. Wait while Studio reads the local game components and prepares the character through Blender/Sollumz. Check the displayed model and Paint surface before adding artwork. Save your project. Studio remembers the prepared character on this PC. A saved project created through this setup can restore that character automatically when reopened. Each body is prepared on first use. In another new top design, select Set up GTA character to reuse the prepared body; the app does not silently replace an existing original garment or reinterpret its artwork. For jackets, dresses and other item types, use the matching GTA item browser to select the garment you actually want. The character cache belongs to this app profile on this PC. It is not included in project backups, cloud snapshots or the public installer. On another computer, complete setup using that computer's game installation. If a setup-created project has no usable cache, select Load saved GTA character to prepare it again. A custom imported GLB still needs its own original file for relinking. Without the game tools, select Work on an original garment without a character to continue with an original shirt or hoodie pattern. This shows the garment alone. Use a real GTA body later for game-specific fit checks. Choose what you want to make Open Item type in Clothing Studio and select the category that matches your source: Tops, T-shirts and hoodies; jackets and coats; dresses and full outfits. Pants and jeans, shorts, skirts, shoes and sneakers, boots. Hats and caps, helmets, glasses and sunglasses, goggles, masks and face coverings. Gloves and arms, bags and backpacks, undershirts, vests and body armor, badges and decals, or a custom wearable target. Studio shirt/hoodie patterns remain available for learning. Other categories require a matching imported source mesh. For example, choosing Hats & caps sets the relevant prop workflow; it does not turn a T-shirt into a hat. Arbitrary imported clothing still needs suitable skin weights and GTA material setup. Manage artwork from a layer menu In 0.19.1, right-click an artwork layer to duplicate it, copy or paste artwork, raise or lower its order, show or hide it, or remove it. Unavailable actions are disabled. The same menu opens with Shift+F10 or the Menu key when a layer row is focused. These actions edit the artwork layers of the design. Removing a layer does not remove the source garment. Use the studio’s Undo control to reverse an unintended edit during the session. Load a garment Select the intended Item type and fitting body. For the default top, use Set up GTA character . For another garment, choose Edit GTA clothing… to open the GTA item browser directly. If prompted, select your GTA V Legacy installation. Choose a compatible drawable and texture from the choices beneath the preview, then select Edit selected GTA top or Edit selected GTA item . The expandable Fit real GTA clothing panel also retains Browse GTA tops… and Browse GTA items… . Wait for the actual model and paint surface to finish loading. Check Imported garment , Paint surface and the displayed character before adding artwork. The body, item type and browse controls temporarily pause during loading to prevent overlapping requests. For a source already on disk, use Load wearable GLB… or Import GTA components… as appropriate. Choose a file that exists; typing a suggested filename does not download it. The right-hand panel should become Garment UV artwork . Imported custom clothing GLBs are not embedded as a complete retained source inside the project. Keep the original GLB available; a saved binding can ask you to relink it after reopening or moving PCs. Custom files are not silently substituted with the default character merely because their filenames match. Locally catalogued GTA items can reload from the configured game installation. Change the body or item type Choose another Fitting body or Item type . A Custom wearable also exposes its intended GTA wearable slot . If a garment or Blender source is linked, read Change garment or character? . Choose Cancel to keep the current design exactly as it is. Choose Change and keep artwork to detach the current garment, its original diffuse base texture and linked Blender source. Your source files stay on your computer; your added logos, text and other artwork stay in the project. Use Set up GTA character , Edit GTA clothing… or your own compatible source to choose the new garment. Review artwork placement on its UV layout before exporting. Changing the target does not convert or refit the old geometry. A male shirt is not automatically made into a female shirt, and selecting a hat category does not turn it into a hat. The old preview is cleared so it cannot be mistaken for the newly selected target. Use Undo or Ctrl+Z to restore the previous design and source binding during the session. Recognized local GTA sources can restore their preview; a custom imported GLB may ask you to relink its original file. These controls are temporarily disabled while a model is loading. Place your artwork Choose Add text or Add PNG for artwork you have permission to use. Select the artwork layer and use Place on 3D model when you want to position it on the garment surface. Enable UV seams to see how the flat texture wraps around the model. Keep artwork inside the intended UV region. Rotate the character and inspect the front, sides and back: a design that looks centered on the flat image can cross a seam or land on another part of the garment. Reuse an artwork layer Select a text or PNG layer in Artwork layers . Choose Duplicate to make an independent layer at the same position, then move or edit that copy. Choose Copy layer , open another clothing project, and choose Paste layer to reuse it there. The copied layer keeps its text or embedded PNG, size, position, rotation, opacity and mirroring. This is a local clipboard inside the running app, not the Windows clipboard or a saved preset library. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V use it when the clothing workspace is focused; typing fields keep ordinary text-copy behavior. Clothing Undo / Redo survives switching workspaces in the current session. Reopening the app starts a new Undo history; save or checkpoint work you want to keep. The design still has one artwork stack and selected paint material, not independent artwork stacks for every material. Apply a saved fit without losing newer edits In Fitting, choose a supported saved GTA garment and save any current source-design edits before applying its fit. In 0.19.3, completion keeps newer unsaved script or design edits made while the fit save was running. The saved fit and project revision are reconciled without reloading an older editor snapshot. If you independently change the source or fit, those newer changes remain yours. Save again when the project still shows unsaved work. Recheck the fit on the intended character and validate the final native resource in FiveM. Export and continue Export PNG texture saves an image. The texture tools also provide Build texture YTD and Retexture existing YTD… for their supported texture-dictionary workflows. A texture does not contain the garment's mesh or rig. For geometry or rig changes, choose Edit mesh in Blender… . Save your Blender edits and use Refresh from Blender to inspect the updated source. Pack Builder handles the relevant native component workflow; the finished wearable still needs in-game testing. If the body pokes through the shirt, check that you loaded the intended garment and character combination. Enlarging artwork or changing fabric color cannot repair a mesh-fitting problem.
headings: Choose the right source Set up your first GTA character Choose what you want to make Manage artwork from a layer menu Load a garment Change the body or item type Place your artwork Reuse an artwork layer Apply a saved fit without losing newer edits Export and continue

title: Create jewelry and import chains
summary: Work with chains and pendants, size watches or rings, fit bracelets, grills and earrings, and prepare supported sources for export.
body: Choose your jewelry type In a Studio-pattern design, open Jewelry type and choose Necklace / pendant , Bracelet , Watch , Ring , Grill / teeth caps , Earring or Custom imported jewelry . Watches, bracelets, rings, grills and earrings have editable geometry and size controls. Use the relevant attachment controls for the left/right side, ring finger, or upper/lower jaw. Detail isolates the piece for editing; Worn shows its fitting reference. Inspect the piece from more than one angle. These are editable starting patterns. A different character can need different fitting and rigging, and the preview does not establish in-game behavior. Switch types without losing the fit Each jewelry type remembers its own dimensions, attachment choice and position/rotation. For example, set a ring’s diameter and finger, switch to Watch, then return to Ring to continue with the saved ring settings. These settings persist in the local project and its backup. Reset dimensions resets size controls only; it keeps the chosen attachment and placement. Reset fit offsets resets position and rotation without changing the selected side, finger or jaw. Changing type stays within one project. Material finishes and imported source models remain shared design settings; use Duplicate / Save as for independently named designs. Jewelry Undo / Redo survives a visit to another workspace during the current app session, but restarting begins a new Undo history. Inspect imported parts with a right-click In 0.19.1, right-click a part in the imported model’s part list to show or hide it, show all parts, or frame the model. Focus the row and use Shift+F10 or the Menu key for keyboard access. Hide part from model and export affects both the jewelry preview and supported export of the imported model. Recheck the visible parts before exporting; choose Show all parts to bring hidden parts back. In 0.19.2: Right-click a visible mesh in an imported jewelry model to open its part actions directly. Fitting-body geometry is not an editable jewelry part. Right-drag still controls the camera; dragging, pointer cancellation and releasing outside the canvas do not open a menu. Blank canvas provides applicable frame/show-all actions. Focus the canvas and use Shift+F10 for keyboard access. Start with an existing model This workflow is available in public alpha 0.21.0. You do not have to model every link yourself: Jewelry Studio can open a compatible chain GLB that you have permission to use. Keep the original download and its license information. A downloadable model may include attribution requirements, and permission to use it does not necessarily mean you can redistribute the original asset as part of your own library. Import and frame the chain Open a Jewelry Studio design and choose Import chain GLB… . Select the actual downloaded .glb file. Use Model and Frame model to inspect the complete import. Check its shape before adjusting its fit. Set Imported chain size . This measures the longest visible dimension in centimeters; it is not a necklace circumference measurement. Adjust the position and rotation fields to orient the model. Use Front , Side and Back to avoid judging the fit from only one angle. A successful import should show the filename and a visible mesh count. If everything disappears, check whether all parts are hidden before importing again. Inspect parts and finish Open Model parts to hide a display stand, plaque or other unwanted object included in the source. Hidden parts are omitted from the mesh export, so inspect that list before saving your final result. Show all parts restores their visibility. Material tint changes the model's color presentation. It does not turn a rough, nonmetallic source material into a properly authored metallic GTA shader. Reset placement and tint restores the imported-chain placement defaults. Worn uses a studio fitting character for a provisional visual check. That preview is not a rigged GTA ped result. Keep newer work when a fit save finishes For a supported saved GTA accessory, use Fitting to apply its adjustment back to the source project. Save current source edits before starting. In 0.19.3, a completed fit save preserves edits made while it was running instead of reloading an old project snapshot. An independently changed source or fit is not overwritten, and a reply cannot replace another open project. If the project still shows unsaved changes, save them normally. Undoing an applied fit follows the same protection. These checks preserve editable work; they do not prove the accessory's in-game rigging or appearance. Choose an export path Export mesh and Save .blend preserve source work for the next stage. A generic unbound chain or custom GLB still needs suitable GTA rigging, materials and native conversion. Supported rigid accessory categories provide explicit attachment targets; they do not make every arbitrary model game-ready. For an existing GTA accessory, use Browse GTA jewelry to choose compatible local necklace, wrist or ear assets, then use the selected accessory. This reads permitted assets from your own Legacy installation. It is a different starting point from a generic chain download. Pack Builder uses the supported component or prop target. Test the finished wearable on its intended character, including wrist/hand movement, fingers, jaw motion and combinations with clothing. Keep the editable source and a project backup so you can correct the fit and rebuild.
headings: Choose your jewelry type Switch types without losing the fit Inspect imported parts with a right-click Start with an existing model Import and frame the chain Inspect parts and finish Keep newer work when a fit save finishes Choose an export path

title: Customize an imported vehicle
summary: Bring a real GTA vehicle into the workshop, inspect its parts and prepare a native source before building a pack.
body: Choose your source Vehicle Studio is included in public alpha 0.21.0. The original sample coupe teaches selection and navigation, but it is not a rigged GTA vehicle. Use Load GTA Blista… to read that vehicle from your own GTA V Legacy installation. For another compatible car, choose Import GTA fragment… and supply its base YFT and matching texture dictionaries. Import vehicle GLB… accepts a supported general model; a GLB by itself does not provide all native vehicle behavior. Inspect before editing In Model , choose Frame vehicle to see the whole car. Select a part in the hierarchy or viewport. Use Frame selected for a close look, and visibility controls to inspect what lies underneath. Read the model-source information and any Check & learn messages. Resolve missing textures with the matching source YTDs. Save the project before experimenting with appearance or native-source changes. The static inspection model lets you examine geometry and parts. It does not simulate driving, damage, doors or suspension in the GTA engine. Inspect vehicle parts with a right-click In 0.19.1, right-click a row in Parts to show or hide that part, or choose Show all parts . A focused row supports Shift+F10 or the keyboard Menu key. These controls change preview visibility so you can inspect the model. They do not remove parts from the linked native vehicle source or establish their in-game visibility. In 0.19.2: Right-click a visible vehicle part to open its actions directly. These commands still affect preview visibility, not the linked native source. Right-drag still controls the camera; dragging, pointer cancellation and releasing outside the canvas do not open a menu. Blank canvas provides applicable frame/show-all actions. Focus the canvas and use Shift+F10 for keyboard access. Make a controlled change Open Customize and try one paint or wheel adjustment. Check clearance from the front and side. For artwork, import a PNG under Livery , choose Place logo on car , then position it on a suitable surface using its UVs. A top-projected logo or preview shader override can look convincing while still requiring a different native treatment. Review the app's diagnostics instead of assuming every viewport material change is ready for export. In Configuration , use a unique spawn name and make small handling changes. Compare them on the same driving route after export. Prepare the native source Open Native workshop . Choose Create .blend from YFT… , or Link vehicle .blend… for a compatible Sollumz source. Use Inspect linked source to examine its bones, collision and detail levels. After editing and saving in Blender, select Refresh model from source . In Build pack , select vehicles with linked sources and choose Build vehicle ZIP… or Build resource folder… . Read the build report and test-drive.txt , then test the stated spawn name in your development server. Check doors, steering, collision, textures and distant LODs in game. Editor triangle counts are geometry statistics, not measured in-game FPS.
headings: Choose your source Inspect before editing Inspect vehicle parts with a right-click Make a controlled change Prepare the native source

title: From project to FiveM resource
summary: Separate editable source, native assets, packaged resources and actual in-game testing.
body: An export can mean different things Choose an output for the next task you want to perform. These stages are related, but they are not interchangeable: Editable project: your Studio library entry or backup. Source output: files such as a PNG texture, GLB mesh or .blend source. These let you continue in another tool. Native GTA assets: converted game-format files produced through a supported workflow. FiveM resource: a named folder with the appropriate assets, scripts and manifest. Tested result: a resource you have actually loaded and checked in a development server. A good-looking viewport proves only that the editor could display the model. Renaming JSON or a GLB file to a GTA extension does not convert it. Export a script resource In Script Studio, save your changes and run Validate . Resolve the listed errors, then choose Export ZIP . Extract the named resource folder, not just its individual files. Check that fxmanifest.lua is directly inside the resource folder. A common mistake is an extra folder level between the resource name and its manifest. Also check required framework resources and any declared dependencies. Build models through the supported pipeline MLO and supported wearable or vehicle workflows can require Blender, Sollumz, CodeWalker and permitted source assets. Follow the diagnostics for the workflow you selected. A general source-mesh export does not add missing game rigging, collision or native metadata automatically. Read the conversion result and inspect the final files before packaging. Missing textures, failed conversions or unresolved dependencies should be fixed before you call the resource ready for testing. Replace an exported file deliberately When exporting over an existing file, Studio checks that the chosen destination has not changed while the export was preparing. In 0.19.3, simultaneous exports to the same destination are ordered so a stale replacement cannot silently overwrite another completed export. If you see The destination changed. Choose Export again. , inspect the file that is already there, then export again or choose another filename. Canceling or failing an export does not authorize replacing a newer file. A completed file still needs the appropriate content and in-game checks. Test the actual exported resource For a prepared resource, place its named folder in your dedicated development server’s resources directory. Follow the official resource-command instructions to refresh and start it, with dependencies already running. Join the server and check the behavior that matters: commands respond, models appear, textures load, wearables fit, or interiors have usable floors, entrances and visibility. Record failures separately from editor validation. Save an editable project backup so you can fix the source and rebuild.
headings: An export can mean different things Export a script resource Build models through the supported pipeline Replace an exported file deliberately Test the actual exported resource

title: Set up Blender and Sollumz
summary: Check the external tools used for native assets and move between an editable source and the app's preview.
body: What each tool does Brick by Script provides the project workspace and beginner-facing tools. Blender supplies detailed modeling and source-file editing. Sollumz adds the GTA-oriented asset workflow inside Blender. CodeWalker is used for supported asset inspection or conversion steps where that workflow requires it. You can learn the core editors without completing every native-tool setup first. Producing your own native game asset is the point where the selected pipeline's dependencies matter. Check your installation Install Blender and follow the official Sollumz setup documentation for a compatible combination. Enable the add-on and any native export provider required by your chosen workflow. In MLO Studio, open Blender tools , or use Build and test → Check build tools . Read the Blender and GTA tools results. If the intended Blender installation was not detected, choose Choose blender.exe . After changing the installation or add-ons, select Check again . Resolve the specific issue shown before trying a native build. The tool check reports detected versions and availability. Keep that information with a build report so a later failure can be compared with the tool combination that produced the earlier result. Keep source and preview in sync In MLO Studio, Export Blender source creates an editable Blender source. The result offers Continue in Blender . A saved .blend is source work, not a finished FiveM resource. In Clothing Studio, use the Blender workspace. Create Blender source… prepares the selected input; Open in Blender lets you edit it; Refresh from Blender reads the saved result. When importing GTA clothing through Sollumz, the workspace requests the local YDD with its matching skeleton YFT, and a YTD when textures are needed. Vehicle Studio uses Native workshop with Create .blend from YFT… or Link vehicle .blend… . Save changes in Blender before refreshing the app's model. Use CodeWalker when needed The GTA tools dialog includes Choose CodeWalker , Open CodeWalker and Convert native / XML . Follow the supported conversion result and instructions for your specific files. Merely renaming JSON, XML or a generic mesh to a GTA extension does not convert the asset. Keep source files and referenced textures together when moving projects. See projects and backups , then review the export checklist before packaging.
headings: What each tool does Check your installation Keep source and preview in sync Use CodeWalker when needed

title: Test a resource in FiveM
summary: Test the exact exported resource, record what happened and keep engine validation separate from an editor preview.
body: Choose the build to test A successful conversion or package check means the build passed those checks. It does not prove that a player can enter the interior, wear the accessory or drive the vehicle correctly. Use a development server you control and keep the exported ZIP with its build report. Follow the installation instructions included with that build. Extract the actual resource folder into the server's resources directory; the manifest should be inside that resource folder, not buried under an extra archive wrapper. For resource structure, consult the official FiveM manifest reference . Resolve required dependencies and server-console errors before judging the model itself. Record an interior walkthrough In the MLO project's Build and test workspace, find Manual FiveM client tests . Choose Choose tested ZIP and select the exact resource ZIP installed on the server. The app records its SHA-256 fingerprint. Enter the FiveM client or game build you are testing. Join the development server, visit the exported map location and perform each check. Mark it Passed , Failed or Not applicable based on what you actually observed. Leave unperformed checks as Not tested . An unavailable staircase is different from a staircase that failed its test. What to check in the game Enter through the front door and walk through every doorway. Walk on all floors, check wall collision and use each staircase where present. Look through every portal from both directions and move through the entire interior again. Inspect textures, flickering surfaces, furniture and missing props. For a vehicle, use the spawn name from the build's test-drive instructions. Check steering, doors, collision, materials and LOD changes at distance, then compare handling on a repeatable route. For clothing and jewelry, test on the intended character and look for clipping or deformation during movement. Save evidence and retest changes Write repeatable observations in Walkthrough notes : where the problem occurs, the viewing direction and the steps needed to reproduce it. Select Save walkthrough report to keep the record with that build. Open walkthrough report previews an existing report. Restoring its results requires the matching ZIP. Choosing a different ZIP starts a new walkthrough; save the old report first if you need it. Editing the building or its placement clears the current test record because the old answers no longer describe the same result. The app's public release has not established universal in-game acceptance. Your own resource, dependencies and environment still need this validation.
headings: Choose the build to test Record an interior walkthrough What to check in the game Save evidence and retest changes

title: What’s new in 0.21.0
summary: 18 practical studio lessons, pinned practice and a tools-and-models setup guide.
body: 0.21.0 — Learn by making Six studio learning paths add 18 practical lessons, saved practice progress, knowledge checks and a collapsible lesson panel beside your work. Existing Lua lessons remain available. Explore the learning paths or find tool downloads and male/female character setup . The setup guide covers every studio and points to official or developer-linked sources. 0.20.2 — Find your files. Keep creating. Browse your own files: Add resource file now opens the Windows file picker through Browse files… . Select an existing text file, review its project destination and add its contents. Existing paths are protected; your original file stays unchanged. Keep text intact: imports and editor changes preserve Unicode, existing UTF-8 byte-order marks and line endings. Cancelling the picker keeps your current selection; Use empty file returns the dialog to blank-file creation. A clothing button that opens the browser: Edit GTA clothing… now starts the GTA item browser directly and reveals the choices beneath the preview. Change the fitting target: Item type, Fitting body and the custom GTA slot can be changed after loading a garment. A confirmation explains what will be unlinked. Your text and logos stay, and Undo restores the previous design. Keep the preview in step: changing targets clears the old model instead of leaving the previous garment visible. Loading briefly disables these controls to prevent overlapping requests. Changing a target selects a different workflow; it does not convert the old mesh into another body or item. Choose a matching garment and review your artwork’s placement. Custom GLB previews may need their original files relinked after Undo. Source files are not deleted. Follow Add a file from your computer or Change the body or item type . 0.20.1 — Start with the character you will use Clothing Studio now begins with a guided Set up GTA character flow for the real male and female freemode bodies. The old bundled fitting person no longer appears in this workspace. No GLB hunt: choose your GTA V Legacy installation and use the existing Blender/Sollumz and CodeWalker pipeline to prepare the character locally. Prepare once per body: Studio keeps the prepared model in this PC's app profile. Use it in a new top design by selecting Set up GTA character. Saved projects created through setup can restore their character automatically. Keep custom garments yours: setup does not silently replace original garment designs, custom GLB bindings, jackets or other clothing categories with a default tee. Existing GLB and component imports remain available. Keep creating without a character: original shirt and hoodie patterns remain available as a garment-only workspace. Game assets are not included in the installer or project backups. Another PC needs its own game installation and character setup. See the character setup steps and creative tool setup . 0.20.0 — Make room for your next idea Midnight Showroom brings the blue Brick by Script identity into the working desktop app, with navy panels, clearer navigation and a gallery of your own saved work. All five studios and your existing local project library remain available. A shared top bar: use Home, Projects, Studios, Tools and Learn, with command search and settings alongside them. Home and the project library share a New project chooser for all five project types. Resume with a real preview: Home shows the current project and recent work. Previews come from supported saved app viewports and stay in a bounded local cache. They do not upload source assets or become project backups. A clearer project library: browse a gallery, filter by studio or folder, and keep favorites, tags, selection, context menus, recoverable Trash and recovery actions. Settings that stay organized: a category sidebar, live workspace preview and reachable Done button keep layout, editor, recovery, tool, account and update controls together. Preferences persist across restarts. Consistent studio surfaces: darker panels and a calmer vehicle stage use the same theme without changing imported geometry or paint. Safer everyday details: editing shortcuts do not act on a model while focus is inside the new navigation menus. Notifications and menus are excluded from saved preview captures; favorite, rename and organization actions retain an unchanged project’s preview. Start with the new navigation , saved project previews or workspace settings . Beginner examples and backup commands remain on Home below the recent-project gallery. 0.19.3 — Protect the work you just did This update fixes reliability problems found in an audit and checked again by different reviewers. It keeps the editing tools introduced in earlier versions while improving how the app handles delayed work, recovery and everyday controls. Keep newer edits: delayed MLO imports and completed fitting saves preserve changes made while the operation was running. Imports cannot replace another project's scene, and Undo returns to the actual scene before the import. Keep results tied to their source: MLO builds and design proposals identify the saved scene used. Mesh results check their source and calculation settings; walkthrough exports check the requesting project. Recover intact work: a valid checkpoint can restore a new copy even when the latest project record is damaged. The original stays unchanged, and invalid checkpoints are still rejected. Avoid stale output replacements: competing exports to one destination no longer silently replace each other's completed files. Edit collisions consistently: primitive-only scenes keep their valid format, and generated architectural objects support collision authoring. Use everyday controls more comfortably: dialogs focus their intended fields, library search regains typing focus after initial loading, open dialogs block global project shortcuts, and keyboard-selected palette commands scroll into view. Read recover a damaged project , MLO background results and dialogs and commands for practical guidance. 0.19.2 — Pick up where you left off Reopen a project with its tabs, active file, text selection, cursor, editor scroll and last project workspace restored. These navigation preferences stay on this computer and survive restarting the app. Save your project normally; navigation metadata is not a backup or a cloud upload. Use arrow keys, Home/End and type-ahead in Explorer. Shift-click or Shift+arrow selects project ranges, Ctrl-click toggles a project, and Ctrl+A selects the visible list while it has focus. Text fields retain normal text selection. Right-click visible MLO geometry, vehicle parts and imported jewelry meshes for their existing actions. Right-drag still controls the camera. Blank space offers applicable frame/show-all actions. Vehicle visibility is preview-only; hidden imported jewelry parts affect its supported export. Search now reaches beyond 100 results with Previous/Next. Library Refresh/Retry, Clear filters, Clear selection and named Trash confirmation make the scope of your next action clearer. Dialog titles are accessible, and protected manifest actions are disabled before an invalid operation. Read resume and navigate and select project ranges . 0.19.1 — Keep useful actions within reach Right-click a project, script file or folder to see the actions for that item. Library actions include opening, renaming, duplication, favorites, folder/tags, recovery and recoverable Trash. Explorer keeps New file, relative-path copying and file management close to the selected row. The code editor has Cut, Copy and Paste. Normal text fields provide native text-editing menus. File tabs can close individually, close others, close to the right or close together, then reopen from session history. Use Ctrl+W , Ctrl+Shift+T and Ctrl+Tab , or middle-click a tab. Closing a file tab preserves its unsaved text. MLO hierarchy menus expose framing, duplication, copy/paste, grouping, visibility, locking, isolation and deletion confirmation. Clothing artwork layers provide duplication, copy/paste, ordering and visibility. Imported jewelry parts can be hidden from both the model and export; Vehicle Studio part menus control preview visibility. Focus a supported row and press Shift+F10 or the Menu key to open its menu. Arrow keys move between available actions; Escape dismisses it. Read everyday Script Studio editing and project actions . 0.19.0 — Your workspace, on your terms The settings screen now uses the app’s blue blueprint design. Arrange workspace panels with an immediate preview, change editor preferences and find recovery, tools, accounts and updates in clearly separated sections. Read Make the workspace yours . Optional GitHub sign-in adds private cloud snapshots: save a chosen project, then download an independent local copy using the same account on another PC. Conflicting saves are blocked so you can review both copies. You control uploads, cloud-project deletion and cleanup of interrupted transfers. This is explicit snapshot transfer, not automatic sync. The preview has a 512 MiB reserved-storage allowance per account, including older versions. Local editing remains available without an account. See Continue on another PC for the full workflow and limits. 0.18.0 — Update without leaving the app Open App updates from Workspace settings or the command palette. Check for a newer release, read its notes, download with progress and cancellation, then choose Install and restart when you are ready. Downloads are checked against the published size and SHA-256 before installation. Optional startup checks never download or install automatically. Choose whether to include preview releases, and use clear retry messages for offline access, rate limits or failed downloads. The installed Windows x64 app supports installation; portable and development copies explain that the setup installation is required. Older releases need one manual installer update to gain this feature. See Update the app . 0.17.1 — More control over your projects Open Project library with Ctrl+O to rename, duplicate, favorite, tag and organize designs with folder labels. Search and filter across studios, then sort by name or recent activity. Move one or several projects to recoverable Trash and restore them later. Dependency checks protect collections and server jobs that still use a project. A project copy keeps the current editor active until you open the new copy. See project management . Keep useful versions and reuse your edits Name and pin recovery checkpoints. Library recovery restores the selected project’s saved revision as a new copy. Use Save / Discard / Cancel when switching or closing with autosave off, or explicitly discard unsaved edits from the command palette. Rename, move, duplicate and remove script files or folders through Explorer. Removal creates a checkpoint first. Keep Clothing and Jewelry Undo when visiting another workspace during the same app session. Duplicate a clothing artwork layer, or copy and paste it into another design. Switch jewelry types without losing each type’s dimensions and fitting settings. Reset dimensions leaves attachment and placement intact. Start with Recover work and use Undo or the script file controls . More clothing and jewelry starting points The 0.17.0 expansion is included in this release. Clothing Studio adds category-based workflows for pants, shoes, boots, hats, helmets, glasses, goggles, masks and other wearables alongside tops. Non-top categories start from a matching permitted source mesh; selecting a category does not generate every possible garment. Jewelry Studio adds editable watches, bracelets, rings, grills and earrings alongside necklaces and pendants. Use dimension and attachment controls, then inspect the fit. Read the clothing guide and jewelry guide for the actual source and export requirements. What is tested, and what still needs checking See the 0.21.0 release notes for the checks performed on the exact downloadable build. File browsing, text preservation, target changes, cancellation, Undo and reopening are separate checks from native asset conversion or gameplay. The earlier 0.20.0 development and packaged desktop walkthroughs covered all five creation choices, navigation, context menus, saved previews, settings persistence, project reopening and source-file integrity using isolated projects. Those historical results are not a claim that every workflow was retested for this update. The app remains an unsigned alpha . This update does not establish clean-laptop, hosted sign-in, cross-device transfer or FiveM gameplay acceptance. Test the final exported resource in FiveM before relying on it. Get the current public alpha On an updater-enabled installation, follow Update the app . Otherwise download the Windows installer , save your work, close the older app and run the installer. Follow Install on Windows for setup and verification. The GitHub release includes the published notes and checksums.

title: Troubleshoot your first problem
summary: Find the failing stage, make a small correction and check the result without losing your project.
body: Identify the failing step Write down what you were trying to do and the exact message. Was the failure during installation, opening a project, importing a model, exporting, or running the resource in FiveM? Fix the first failed stage before continuing to the next. Check your app version against the guide’s label. These guides describe public alpha 0.21.0. Update an older installation before looking for controls added in later releases. Save a project backup before experimenting with major changes. When reporting a problem, share the version, reproduction steps and a useful screenshot. Review logs before sharing them and remove credentials or unrelated personal information. A file is missing or validation fails Manifest error: compare the declared path with the actual file, including its folder, spelling and capitalization. A file named client/main.lua needs a matching declaration. Import dialog says “File not found”: select a file that exists on disk. Typing a suggested model filename does not create or download it. Missing textures or linked assets: restore the expected files, check the project’s dependency information and prepare a complete transfer when changing PCs. Export is blocked: open the problem list, fix the reported errors and validate again. An output filename is not a completed export. A project is missing, Trash is blocked or Undo changed Missing from the library: clear search, type, folder and Favorites filters. Then check the Trash tab. Cannot move to Trash: read the named collection or server-job dependency, remove that reference and retry. Cannot duplicate: check linked source files and the selected Blender installation. A duplicate with linked sources needs independent packed copies. Cannot pin a checkpoint: unpin an older point or save a separate backup. Existing pinned history is kept when a pin limit is reached. Undo unavailable after reopening: creator Undo is session history, not saved project history. Use the saved design, a recovery point or a backup. Discard says the project changed: a newer edit arrived while the operation was waiting. It was kept; review the current design before retrying. Follow Recover work and use Undo for the complete steps. A model or native build is not right First confirm the imported model and its scale, orientation, materials and references. A fitting preview is not a guarantee of finished rigging. For native builds, check that the required tools and compatible workflow are available before changing the geometry. In setup, Check installed tools inspects the selected Blender/Sollumz workflow. Choose blender.exe and Choose CodeWalker let you select the intended installations. Tool detection alone does not verify game compatibility. Use help, then report a reproducible issue Open Home → Why is this broken? for the practice repair workflow, or Search help and documentation to find an explanation and an official reference. If the problem remains, use the GitHub issue tracker . Include the smallest set of steps that reproduces it and say whether the failure happens in the app or in FiveM. Do not attach someone else’s protected model files just to demonstrate a bug.

title: Creator glossary
summary: Plain-language definitions for the terms you will encounter across the studios.
body: Projects and code Project: the editable work stored by Brick by Script. Keep a backup if you want to restore or move it. Resource: a named folder that FiveM can start and stop. Manifest: the fxmanifest.lua file that declares a resource’s scripts, files and other information. Client and server: the player’s game and the server process. Lua code must run on the side where its required functions and data exist. NUI: a web-based interface displayed by the game, such as a menu or HUD. Models and materials Mesh: a model’s connected geometry. Vertices are points, edges connect points, and faces form surfaces. Normal: a direction associated with a face or vertex, used in shading and surface orientation. UV layout: a mapping from a model’s surface to a flat texture. Place artwork on the correct UV area to make it appear on the intended part. Material: settings that control a surface’s appearance. A texture is an image used by a material. Rig and skin weights: bones and their influence on mesh vertices. They help an accessory or garment move with a character. GLB: a common model exchange format. It is useful for supported imports and source exports, but is not itself a native GTA drawable. Interiors and performance Collision: geometry that determines where the player or another object can physically move. MLO room: an interior room definition used by the game, separate from the visible wall geometry. Portal: a visibility connection between rooms or between a room and the exterior. A visible doorway and a portal are different things. Archetype: a reusable asset definition. Placement data refers to that definition when putting an instance in the world. LOD: level of detail; alternate detail levels can reduce rendering work at a distance. Draw call: a rendering request. Editor counts and memory estimates help investigate complexity, but are not measured in-game FPS. Build status Source export means editable output for another tool. Native conversion means producing the required game-format files. Packaging gathers the required files into a resource. In-game validation checks the result in an actual FiveM session. Learn how these stages fit together in From project to FiveM resource .
